newsitem.title: GUATEMALA: Guatemala will initiate tariff reductions in 1997.
newsitem.headline: Guatemala will initiate tariff reductions in 1997.

text.p: Guatemala in January will begin a two-year program to significantly reduce tariffs, including a new regime on products imported from elsewhere in Central America, the Economy Minister said Tuesday.

"With this program, we are allowing the productive sector to remain competitive with reductions in duties on raw materials that Costa Rica and El Salvador have already implemented," Juan Mauricio Wurmser told reporters.
Wurmser said the program stems from a resolution adopted by the five nations of Central America last year.
Under the program, tariffs on raw materials produced outside Central America will be reduced from 5 percent to 1 percent the first of the year and will go down to zero within the next few years.
Duties on raw materials produced with Central America will drop from 10 percent to nine percent in January 1997 to seven percent in January 1998 and to five percent a year later.
Tariffs on finished goods come down from 20 percent to 19 percent in January, 17 percent a year later and 15 percent in January 1999.
Wurmser said all of the other countries in Central America already have announced their reduction programs, each with a different schedule.
"The tariff production program assumed by the government will be gradual and progressive," Wurmser said. "We are not bringing in any distorting element that could favor one of the other countries."

According to Wurmser, the government will make up for lost revenues from tariffs through privatization of state-owned businesses next year and through more efficient collection of existing taxes and tariffs.
